host_timing_note: Measured on the FreeRTOS POSIX port, where every task is a thread of a Linux process. Times, jitter and latencies are those of the host's scheduler and are not what the same code shows on a microcontroller. The contents, orderings and sizes of protocol data, and the frames and bytes an exchange takes, do not depend on the host. What happens in a stretch of time does: the jobs and frames of a run of fixed length, ticks dropped, jobs released early; and a stall of the host past the node's 500 ms watchdog or a 1 s protocol timer fails what the node would have passed. Such a failure is never hidden (the bench counts and keeps it, or writes no result), and no stall makes a check pass, so a count of 0 failures holds whatever the host did. The recovery sequence (128 x 11 bit times on an idle bus) and the other figures marked "model" are the controller model's own times and do not depend on the host; the hold-off is the node's policy, timed by the FreeRTOS tick; every figure marked "host" is when the host ran the hardware thread, the node's tasks or the observer, and says nothing about a microcontroller.

config.bus: idle: no frames but the node's own

fault_actions.short: can.fault short, then can.fault none once can.status shows the bus off

fault_to_bus_off.what: the wait for a frame to send under the fault (the node's schedule) and the destroyed attempts (model)

passive_to_bus_off.what: the destroyed attempts of an error-passive transmitter (model; under tx_errors of the frames the node had in its mailboxes, its schedule), and a start a late pass moved or a frame loaded into an idle bus (host); passive_to_bus_off_exact: neither of the last two (model_exact())

bus_off_report_lag.to: the pass that carried it out
bus_off_report_lag.what: how late the hardware thread ran

bus_off_to_driver.what: the pass, the simulated interrupt and the transmit task

holdoff.what: the hold-off (100 ms) of app/can_io.c, on the tick

request_to_count.what: the wake-up of the hardware thread

recovery_report_lag.to: the pass that carried it out
recovery_report_lag.what: how late the hardware thread ran

recovery_to_driver.what: the pass, the simulated interrupt and the transmit task

active_to_first_submit.to: the first frame in a mailbox
active_to_first_submit.what: the driver loads the mailboxes again

first_frame_on_bus.from: the first frame in a mailbox
first_frame_on_bus.what: arbitration and the length (model) of whichever frame the node sent first (its schedule), and a start a late pass moved (host)

first_frame_write_lag.what: how late the hardware thread ran

bus_off_to_active.what: hold-off, host and the recovery sequence

removal_to_active.what: short: the rest of the hold-off, host and the recovery sequence; tx_errors: the fault ends at the bus off

removal_to_first_frame.to: the first frame's end of frame (model)

bus_off_to_dtc.what: the health task's period (100 ms) and the host

dtc_heal.what: 50 health periods without a bus off, and the host
